correctness.rationale: Independent proof check of RESULT.md lines 31–67: telescoping the independent avoidance probabilities gives x/N and x(y−1)/(N(N−1)) for x<y. Subtracting the marginal product gives the stated off-diagonal entries; the diagonal check gives Σ=N D/(N−1)−H/[N(N−1)], with H the inverse of the Dirichlet path difference matrix A. On the interior grid, B=A diag(x(N−x)) is self-adjoint in the weighted inner product; its action on the degree-d quotient of the polynomial flag is (d+1)(d+2), including the one-site grid. Inversion and conjugation give the claimed simple spectrum; the Rayleigh quotient gives both extremal weights. The finite normalized kernel and diagonal terms converge by Riemann sums. In the continuous problem −[t(1−t)p]'' preserves the polynomial flag with the same leading coefficient and is symmetric by integration by parts on t(1−t)p; weighted polynomial density gives completeness. The lower bound is attained by constants and the upper bound is sharp by high-degree modes. The variance bounds are then Rayleigh quotients and the continuum claims direct Riemann-sum and Jacobi consequences. The result is correct, but the frozen claim does not establish a distinct result beyond these direct implications.
